newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Record capex planned for S.African ports - report.
newsitem.headline: Record capex planned for S.African ports - report.

text.p: State transport concern, Transnet, has approved a record capital budget of almost 1.5 billion rand for South Africa's seven commercial ports in 1997/98, Business Day newspaper said on Thursday.
Portnet figures show capital expenditure rose to 654 million rand in 1996/97 from 185 million rand in 1993/94, the bulk of which was spent on upgrading port facilities, the paper said.

It quoted Portnet chief executive Ivor Funnell as saying on Wednesdday that the sharp rise in Portnet's capital investment to 1.44 billion rand was largely due to increased demand after the opening up of international markets following South Africa's democratisation.
The country held its first ever multi-party elections in April 1994.

"Portnet believes that significant investments are required over the short to medium term to cater for the demands and needs of international trade. We have been increasing our capex over the last few years as a result of this trend and it is expected capital investment will continue at about the same level as budgeted for 1997/98," the paper quoted Funnell as saying.
Major projects included the extension of the general cargo bay at Richards Bay and the construction of a drydock facility, coal export terminal and liquid bulk storage facility.
At Durban, projects underway included development of a car terminal at Cato Creek, increasing the container terminal's capacity and improving the Point's city terminal.

The stacking areas were being enlarged at Port Elizabeth and the container rail transfer area upgraded while other projects -- such as a new industrial port at Coega -- were planned to meet future needs.

In Cape Town an additional 400 reefer points had been installed at the container terminal, the expansion of the Duncan Dock cold store had been approved and the combi terminal was being expanded and upgraded.
Projects earmarked at Saldanha included the reclamation of additional land for port development, the construction of a terminal to accommodate the Saldanha Steel project and additional dredging.
